whatItDoes: Increase Pueblo’s sales and use tax rate by 0.25 percentage points beginning January 1, 2027. The question authorizes $5,878,267 in the first full fiscal year and whatever the tax produces afterward. Money would go into a special fund used only for the fire department and technology related to public safety in the city. The city could keep and spend this revenue outside the constitutional and other legal revenue limits identified in the question.
yesMeans: Approve the additional public-safety sales and use tax, dedicated fund and revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this additional tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Add a 0.167% city sales tax for five years, January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2031, to pay only for operating and improving the Pueblo Zoo. The question authorizes up to $3,769,615 in the first full fiscal year and whatever the tax produces afterward during its term. Revenue would go into a special fund and could be kept and spent outside the constitutional and other legal revenue limits identified in the question.
yesMeans: Approve the five-year zoo sales tax, dedicated fund and revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this additional zoo tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Waive the library district’s 5.25% statutory property-tax revenue growth limit for every future property-tax year so it can receive the full revenue produced by its already approved property-tax rate. The district could collect, keep and spend all revenue above legal revenue limits. The measure does not ask voters to increase the property-tax rate.
yesMeans: Approve the continuing property-tax growth-limit waiver and authority to retain and spend district revenue above legal limits.
noMeans: Do not approve this proposed waiver of the district’s property-tax and other revenue limits.

whatItDoes: Permanently extend Pueblo West Metropolitan District’s existing 1% sales tax, which is now scheduled to expire December 31, 2030, at the same rate. The question authorizes $5 million in annual tax revenue and any additional amount the tax produces later. Money and investment income would be used only for fire protection: firefighters and staff, equipment and other capital needs, and constructing, operating and maintaining fire facilities. The district could keep and spend the revenue outside the stated constitutional and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Make the existing 1% fire-protection sales tax permanent and approve the revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not extend the tax beyond its current December 31, 2030 expiration or approve this proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Allow Pueblo West Metropolitan District to keep and spend revenue above the constitutional revenue limit, the statutory 5.5% property-tax revenue growth limit, the 5.25% property-tax limit and other state revenue limits beginning in fiscal year 2026 and continuing afterward. All money above those limits would be used only for its Parks and Recreation Department. This measure would not raise a tax rate or impose a new tax; those would need separate voter approval.
yesMeans: Approve the continuing revenue-limit waivers, with excess revenue restricted to parks and recreation.
noMeans: Do not approve these proposed waivers of the district’s revenue limits.

whatItDoes: Add 11.652 mills to Rye Fire Protection District’s property-tax rate for ten tax years: 2026 through 2035, collected in 2027 through 2036. The question authorizes $1,098,568.97 in the first full fiscal year and whatever the tax produces later during its term. Money would support general district purposes, including emergency staffing and services, equipment, facilities, capital improvements and operating and capital reserves. During those ten years the district could keep and spend the additional tax revenue and investment earnings outside the stated constitutional and state-law limits. The additional levy expires after the stated term unless voters authorize it again.
yesMeans: Approve the ten-year additional property tax and its revenue-limit exception for emergency services and other district purposes.
noMeans: Do not approve this additional property-tax levy or its proposed revenue-limit exception.
